rows.name: National Green Tribunal — its own FAQ says you do not need an advocate
rows.desc_head: The Tribunal states that engaging an advocate is not necessary and that an aggrieved party may approach it in person by submitting an application in the required format — which makes this the cheapest serious forum for stopping a project anywhere in South Asia. Orders bind, and are enforceable with the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure 1908. The gap that ends case

rows.name: AERF — pays private forest owners to keep the trees standing, because buying land in India is hard
rows.desc_head: What it offers a landowner is income from standing forest instead of income from felling it. AERF signs conservation agreements with private forest owners and communities in the northern Western Ghats — open-access forest outside the protected area system, with no legal protection available — and pays incentives against an undertaking not to cut. Its MyForest programme, begun in 2008 on a R

rows.name: CPCB directory of State Pollution Control Boards — find the body that must consent before construction
rows.desc_head: One official directory routes you to the state board that has to consent before anything is built, instead of hunting thirty-five separate sites — the Central Pollution Control Board publishes a dated directory of every State Pollution Control Board and every Union Territory Pollution Control Committee, the current version being as on 1 April 2026. The consent is the chokepoint, and it f

rows.name: People's Science Institute — the Environmental Quality Monitoring Group takes the samples
rows.desc_head: India's answer to the measurement problem: an independent institute with its own Environmental Quality Monitoring Group, which samples and reports rather than campaigning. The model to study is its Ganga work at Haridwar, reported in the Indian press: its scientists took samples from ten drains discharging into the river at the start of the Maha Kumbh, plus river water at three locations, a

rows.name: Goa Foundation — the citizens' body that stopped a state's mining industry in the Supreme Court
rows.desc_head: One writ petition by a citizens' foundation stopped mining across an entire Indian state. Its petition, WP(C) 435 of 2012, built on a commission of inquiry's findings and asked the Supreme Court to direct termination of mining leases where mining had been carried out in breach of the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, the Mines and Minerals Act 1957 and its concession rules, the Environment (P

rows.name: District Mineral Foundation — money already collected for mining-affected people, and the gram sabha approval that governs it
rows.desc_head: This is not money to be raised; it has already been collected, and much of it is unspent. Every mining lease holder pays into the district foundation on top of royalty — 30 per cent of the royalty amount for leases granted before the 2015 amendment and 10 per cent for leases auctioned after it. By November 2024 the foundations held cumulative collections of about 1.02 lakh crore rupees nati

rows.name: Forest Rights Act claims — the gram sabha is the authority, and rejected claims can be revisited
rows.desc_head: Only the forest rights committee and the gram sabha may receive, reject or modify a claim. The ministry's own answers state that a committee including persons who are not members of the gram sabha cannot assist it in discharging its functions on recognition and vesting of forest rights, and that any decision or action by such a committee would be void and have no legal basis. Where a forest

rows.name: Legal Services Authorities — a free panel advocate in every district, up to the Supreme Court
rows.desc_head: Free representation runs from the lowest court to the Supreme Court, and there is no restriction on the kind of case. Under the 1987 statute a state authority exists in every state with institutions below it, panel and retainer advocates are available for court representation at magistrate, sessions, high court and Supreme Court level, and entitlement arises where an applicant meets one of

rows.name: Air pollution complaints — a 24-hour redressal expectation, and proof of action posted back where you filed
rows.desc_head: What it is, and its honest limit. The board's citizen guidelines describe an application through which anyone in the national capital region can lodge an air pollution complaint: register a mobile number and email address, choose the public complaint option, add photographs, and give your name and telephone number. The same application publishes hourly national air quality index values acro

rows.name: DILRMP citizen services — the record of rights, the cadastral map, and revenue court case tracking
rows.desc_head: What can be obtained, and from whom. Under the national land records modernisation programme the department lists the services a citizen can obtain: the record of rights, the cadastral map, spatial data, registration of land and deeds, revenue court case monitoring and transliteration of the record of rights into another language. The programme's stated aims are to modernise land record man

rows.name: RTI — free if they miss the deadline, and a per-day penalty on the officer
rows.desc_head: Ten rupees, thirty days, and forty-eight hours where life or liberty is at stake. Under the 2005 act a citizen may request information from any public authority on written request or by electronic means, with a nominal application fee and no fee at all for applicants below the poverty line. Information is to be provided within thirty days in the ordinary case, and within forty-eight hours w

rows.name: Land Conflict Watch — report your conflict into a verified national database, and look up the comparable ones
rows.desc_head: You can report a conflict into it. The project maintains a database of more than a thousand ongoing land conflicts across the country, with conflicts that are no longer active kept separately as closed, and its site carries a route to report a conflict. For a community whose dispute exists only in local memory and a pile of letters, being recorded in a verified national database means the c

rows.name: Bhuvan — free satellite data, thematic land-use layers, and tools to make your own shapefile
rows.desc_head: Free satellite data, downloadable by period and resolution. The national geoportal provides services and applications built on satellite remote sensing data for public use, including visualisation, three-dimensional exploration of imagery, and free download of satellite datasets for a specified period and resolution; it has run since 2009 and is offered in English, Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.

rows.name: Registered valuers — three asset classes, a searchable register showing status, and the number that must be on the report
rows.desc_head: Land and building is its own registered class. Under the registered valuers and valuation rules of 2017, with the insolvency and bankruptcy board specified as the authority by the central government under the companies legislation, registration as a valuer is granted by asset class — land and building, plant and machinery, and securities or financial assets — each with its own eligibility r

rows.name: Recognised environmental laboratories — the section 12 lists, the named government analyst, and what a tribunal will accept
rows.desc_head: The central board publishes state-wise lists of recognised laboratories. Two sets are maintained: private environmental laboratories recognised under section 12(1)(b) of the environment protection legislation of 1986 with valid recognition, and government, semi-government, public sector and educational institution laboratories recognised under the same provision. The power to grant that rec

rows.name: NHRC complaints — free, tracked by diary number, with a name-display choice and a focal point for defenders
rows.desc_head: Free, online, tracked, and in your own language. Filing a complaint carries no fee. The online system lets the complainant choose whether the matter goes to the national commission or to the state human rights commission for the state where the incident occurred, verifies the mobile number by one-time password, takes the complainant's and victim's details and the incident, allows supporting

rows.name: Prohibited and regulated areas around protected monuments — a hundred metres of no construction, then two hundred needing an NOC
rows.desc_head: A hundred metres in every direction: no new construction. Under the monuments legislation as amended in 2010, the area within a hundred metres of the boundaries of a centrally protected monument is a prohibited area in which no permission is granted for construction, public or private. Repair and renovation of buildings already standing in that band may be permitted, and the competent autho

rows.name: Fair compensation and resettlement law — consent thresholds, a social impact assessment before acquisition, and entitlements for families without land
rows.desc_head: Consent is required where land is acquired for private companies or public-private projects. The fair compensation and transparency legislation of 2013 replaced the colonial-era acquisition statute and applies both to acquisition for the government's own use and to acquisition whose ultimate purpose is transfer to private companies or use in public-private partnership projects. Published of

rows.name: Milaap — no platform fee, no minimum target, and the foreign contribution rule that decides who may donate
rows.desc_head: The platform charges nothing on donations received. Its own pricing and campaign pages state that there are no upfront or fixed fees and no platform fee on donations, with only actual payment processing charges and a voluntary tipping model applying; that there is no time limit on a fundraiser, which can be paused or stopped at any time; that there is no minimum goal to receive funds, so th

rows.name: Coastal Regulation Zone — the state authority, the management plan that fixes the map, and the no development zone distances
rows.desc_head: Every coastal state has an authority whose job includes examining project proposals and preventing violations. Published legal material records that each coastal state and union territory has a state coastal zone management authority, responsible for monitoring compliance, examining project proposals, recommending clearances, preventing violations and updating the coastal zone management pl

rows.name: Tree Officer permission and the heritage tree — fifteen days before any felling, an objection triggers a hearing, and compensatory planting equal to the tree's age
rows.desc_head: In a state with this urban trees legislation, no tree may be felled without the Tree Officer's prior permission — including on the owner's own land. The Act provides that once it is in force in an urban area, notwithstanding any custom, usage, contract or law, no person shall fell a tree or cause one to be felled on any land, whether of his ownership or otherwise, within that area ex

rows.name: Groundwater NOC conditions — the standard terms attached to an abstraction permission, the over-exploited bar, and the meters that must report
rows.desc_head: The conditions attached to a groundwater permission are published, which makes them checkable against what a project is actually doing. A no objection certificate for groundwater abstraction, published with a project's clearance documents, carries standard conditions including that no additional abstraction or de-watering structures shall be constructed without the authority's prior appr

rows.name: Eco-sensitive zones — the buffer round a national park or sanctuary, the sixty-day objection window on the draft notification, and the one-kilometre mining bar
rows.desc_head: Mining is barred within one kilometre of a national park or sanctuary, by order of the Supreme Court. Published legal analysis of the 2023 modification records that mining within a national park or wildlife sanctuary, and within an area of one kilometre from its boundary, shall not be permissible; that the earlier blanket direction does not apply to zones for which draft and final no

rows.name: Community reserves and conservation reserves — land declared on the community's own volunteering, a management committee that can block land use change, and ownership left intact
rows.desc_head: A community reserve is declared because the community volunteered, not because the state took the land. The wildlife legislation provides that the State Government may, where the community or an individual has volunteered to conserve wildlife and its habitat, declare any private or community land not comprised within a national park, sanctuary or conservation reserve as a community reser

rows.name: Wetlands Rules 2017 — the state authority's dated duties, the Brief Document with mapped boundaries, objections before notification, and the activities banned inside a wetland and its zone of influence
rows.desc_head: The state authority's duties come with deadlines a community can hold it to. The 2017 rules provide that the state or union territory wetlands authority shall prepare a list of all wetlands in the state within three months of publication of the rules; prepare a list of wetlands to be notified within six months, taking into account any existing list under state Acts; recommend identified

rows.name: Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate — the two permissions no industry may start or run without, the online system where their status is searchable, and the imprisonment term for operating without them
rows.desc_head: Two consents gate an industry, and both are searchable online. The state boards' online consent management and monitoring systems carry a search status page, letting anyone check the state of a consent application, and explain the framework in their own words: that consent means the board's sanction for the discharge of sewage or trade effluent into a stream, well, sewer or on lan

rows.name: Forest Survey of India — forest cover assessed every two years to district and forest division level, the canopy density classes it uses, and fire alerts sent to registered users by SMS and email
rows.desc_head: Forest cover is assessed biennially and published down to district and forest division. The survey's own report records that it gives forest cover of the country at state, district and forest division level, and changes in forest cover against the previous assessment; that it reports forest cover inside and outside the recorded forest area, in hill districts, in the north-eastern

rows.name: The Habitats Trust Grants — three grant tiers with stated durations, one open to individuals and one written for grassroots conservationists outside any registered body, and the screening a proposal goes through
rows.desc_head: A grant programme funds habitat conservation, and one tier is open to individuals. The trust records the grants as recognising and supporting conservation organisations and individuals who work to conserve the country's natural habitats and native species, especially the lesser-known species and neglected habitats, aiming to support holistic, innovative and replicable conservation

rows.name: Kalpavriksh and the community conserved areas work — a registered action group started by students to save a forest, its CCA documentation portal, and its petitions against orders restricting rights inside protected areas
rows.desc_head: A community's own conserved area can be documented and defended, and one organisation does that work. The group records community conserved areas as natural ecosystems — forest, marine, wetlands, grasslands or others — containing significant wildlife and biodiversity value, conserved by communities for cultural, religious, livelihood or political purposes, using customary laws or other e

rows.name: HRLN — legal aid centres across the states, more than two hundred lawyers, paralegals and activists, crisis-intervention teams and people's tribunals, and free representation for people with no access to the courts
rows.desc_head: A national network of lawyers takes cases free for people who cannot otherwise reach a court. Published description records the organisation, founded in 1989, as having grown from a fledgling law firm to an organisation with legal aid centres in several parts of the country, now a nationwide network of more than 200 lawyers, paralegals and social activists across 26 states and uni

rows.name: SANDRP — a rivers and dams network publishing weekly and annual overviews of hydropower and pumped storage, court orders on project impacts, and analysis a dam-affected community can cite
rows.desc_head: There is a standing network on dams whose published output tracks the projects themselves. The network records itself as an informal network working on issues related to rivers, communities and large scale water infrastructure like dams: their environmental and social impacts, their performance and issues related to governance of rivers and dams, and records its site as an effort

rows.name: mines, minerals & PEOPLE — a national alliance of mining-affected communities, its work on the district mineral fund that mines must pay into, and the consultations it runs on how that money is used
rows.desc_head: Communities living beside mines have a national alliance of their own. The alliance records itself as a growing alliance of individuals, institutions and communities who are concerned and affected by mining, formed because the isolated struggles of different groups pointed to the need for a broad national alliance for combating the destructive nature of mining. For a vi

rows.name: The Environment Monitoring Laboratory — an independent analytical lab for air, water, soil, waste and food contamination, with named instruments, referral services and laboratory training
rows.desc_head: There is an independent laboratory whose stated purpose is producing evidence that pollution is man-made. The laboratory records that it was established to document and scientifically validate the evidence showing the anthropogenic nature of environmental pollution and ecological degradation, following the processes of sampling, analysis and public dissemination of information

rows.name: Environment Support Group — a city and state organisation whose lakes petition produced court-ordered lake protection committees, with named trustees, a published address and free support to communities
rows.desc_head: A city-based organisation's petition ended with the state ordered to devolve lake regulation to local committees. Published reporting records that its lakes petition, filed in 2008 and heard for several years, was decided on 11 April 2012, directing the state to ensure that local communities were involved in lake rehabilitation and management, and that regulation was devolved to lake pro

rows.name: District and taluk legal services authorities — front offices inside the district and taluk courts, panel advocate lists published by district, legal aid clinics in villages, and the right to complain about an assigned lawyer
rows.desc_head: Free legal help is delivered from an office inside the district court, and a second one in the taluk court. A district court records that the authority provides legal aid by way of the services of able, efficient advocates, to any person who fulfils the criteria, and that it functions as the district authority at district level and as taluk committees at taluk level. It record

rows.name: The gram sabha and its ward-level assemblies — roughly 2.5 lakh village panchayats whose plans and accounts the assembly must approve, a published quorum, seven days' notice, and the social audit
rows.desc_head: The village assembly's agenda is the one a community wants to be in the room for. A government economic service record states that the assembly does not have any executive function and operates as a recommending body only, and that it holds meetings normally two to four times a year but can meet as and when necessary, with dates fixed by statute in some states. It records the

rows.name: Taluk and sub-registrar offices — the encumbrance certificate that lists every registered transaction, the mutation hearing where neighbours may object, and the information request that forces a stalled file to move
rows.desc_head: Two different offices hold the two documents a claim needs. A government guide records that the encumbrance certificate relating to any piece of land can be obtained from the sub-registrar's office, while the ownership certificate — the record of rights — has to be applied for and taken from the corresponding taluk office. Published description records the certificate as a

rows.name: Urban ward committees and area sabhas — the city counterpart of the village assembly, seats reserved for citizens and community organisations in one state, and a study naming the cities where they actually meet
rows.desc_head: In one state, the law reserves ward committee seats for citizens and community organisations. A published study records that the state's amended municipal legislation, in a numbered section, gives powers to the state government to nominate seven members to the wards committees — five citizens and one representative each from non-governmental or community-based organisations working in th

rows.name: Sahabat Alam Malaysia — community land mapping and legal support, from two offices only
rows.desc_head: Two offices cover the whole country and which one you write to is decided for you: the Penang headquarters handles Peninsular Malaysia, the Marudi office in Baram handles Sarawak, and there is nothing in Sabah. Founded in 1977, registered under the Societies Act 1966 and a Friends of the Earth International member since 1983, SAM works on indigenous customary rights and the natural resource

rows.name: PACOS Trust — Sabah: they train you to document settlement history for an NCR claim
rows.desc_head: The offer that matters is training in the systematic documentation of indigenous settlement history to support a native customary rights title claim — not a lawyer and not a grant, but the evidence work that decides whether an NCR claim survives, done with a community rather than for it. PACOS also states that it acts as an intermediary between community organisations and outside bodies, wh

rows.name: Jabatan Alam Sekitar — exhibition dates are published, and approving the report is not approving the project
rows.desc_head: The Department publishes each EIA report's public exhibition period and comment deadline as a dated notice, so the dates are knowable in advance rather than something you hear about late. Two live examples show the shape: the Penang Mutiara Line LRT segment 2 report was exhibited from 9 March to 7 April 2026 with public comments accepted until 22 April, and the Lynas rare-earth expansion at

rows.name: Malaysian Nature Society — stopped a golf course, then got handed the park to run
rows.desc_head: The arc worth studying: a state government planned to turn the Kuala Selangor mangrove and mudflat into a golf course, the Society campaigned against it, the area was established as a nature park in 1987 instead, and the Society now manages and runs that park on behalf of the Selangor state government. On its own account this is the only case in Malaysia of a park managed by an NGO for the

rows.name: Sarawak NCR — the five acts that create the right, and why a perimeter survey is not a title
rows.desc_head: Five acts create the right, and the cut-off date is 1 January 1958. The department's own explanation is that native customary rights may be created by felling virgin jungle and occupying the land cleared, by planting the land with fruit trees, by occupation or cultivation, by use of land for a burial ground or shrine, and by use of land of any class for rights of way — and that rights creat

rows.name: MyBar Pro Bono Hub — where an organisation, not an individual, asks for a lawyer
rows.desc_head: The applicant here is the organisation, which solves a problem running through every other legal aid entry in this file. Published accounts of the hub's launch by the bar council's human rights committee record that law firms of any size may register to offer free legal services, that non-governmental organisations submit requests for assistance, and that every case is reviewed by a working

rows.name: NAHRIM water quality laboratory — an accredited lab that states it serves the public, and the agency-only lab behind it
rows.desc_head: An accredited laboratory that says in its own words that it serves the public. The national water research institute's water quality laboratory offers chemical and microbiological analysis across a range of water matrices — drinking water, surface water, effluent and groundwater — holds a numbered accreditation certificate from the national standards department, and states that alongside su

rows.name: National Conservation Trust Fund and the MySDG Trust Fund — a conservation trust, and a fund with two calls a year
rows.desc_head: A national conservation trust fund exists, and its first listed category is protecting particular places. The ministry's national conservation trust fund for natural resources states its purposes as supporting capacity building to meet the country's obligations under multilateral environmental agreements and providing a mechanism to receive and channel funds supporting natural resource mana

rows.name: Jabatan Bantuan Guaman — a public eligibility calculator, plus mediation and a legal companion service
rows.desc_head: You can test your own eligibility before applying. The department, which sits under the prime minister's department, publishes an online means test for legal aid eligibility as a public system, alongside its pages on who qualifies and how to apply. Running that calculator before making an appointment costs nothing and answers the question most communities waste weeks on. Only Korea, among t

rows.name: Carian rasmi and e-Tanah — the title search that carries the registrar's endorsement
rows.desc_head: There are two title searches, and only one carries the registrar's signature. A land office distinguishes the private search from the official search: the official search examines, notes or extracts from any register of title, presentation book, correction book or any instrument of dealing or application delivered to the registrar, is applied for on the official search form issued by the re

rows.name: SPRM and the Whistleblower Protection Act — protection that dies if you go public first
rows.desc_head: Going public first destroys the protection. Under the 2010 whistleblower protection act the identity of a person who discloses improper conduct, and the information they give, are confidential and may not be revealed to anyone — including during proceedings in court — and the discloser cannot be subjected to civil, criminal or disciplinary action as a result of the disclosure. Protection at

rows.name: Ketua Audit Negara — reports published project by project, and an auditor who may read classified documents
rows.desc_head: Reports are published project by project. The auditor general's report portal carries audits organised by ministry and by named project — among them the management of flood mitigation in the capital, a public private partnership redevelopment of a broadcasting complex, an air traffic control centre project and a government electronic services concession. A community facing a comparable sche

rows.name: Yayasan Hasanah — a grant programme with an environment window, and published guidelines each cycle
rows.desc_head: Environment is one of five named funding areas, not an afterthought. The foundation's published grant guidelines set out a grants programme across five impact areas — education, community development, environment, arts and public spaces, and knowledge — with the stated aim of catalysing social impact at scale. For a community group whose work is environmental but whose case is also about la

rows.name: The valuers' board register — check the valuer behind a compensation figure, and where to complain about one
rows.desc_head: A compensation figure is a valuer's opinion, and the valuer is on a public register. The board keeps and maintains the register of valuers, appraisers, estate agents, property managers, probationary valuers and probationary estate agents, together with the register of firms of valuers, appraisers and estate agents, and its site carries a search listing for those registers. When a number is

rows.name: SUHAKAM — a representative may file for the community, it can summon witnesses, and it stops if the matter goes to court
rows.desc_head: Someone can file on the community's behalf. Under the commission's establishing legislation it may inquire into an alleged infringement of human rights on its own motion, or on a complaint made by an aggrieved person or group of persons, or by a person acting on behalf of an aggrieved person or group. Documented practice includes customary landowners lodging a formal complaint through an en

rows.name: Consumers' Association of Penang — a legal section that represents communities, and a complaints desk taking thousands a year
rows.desc_head: There is a legal section whose stated job is representing communities. The association's published description of its own sections records a legal section that handles public interest cases and represents communities in need of legal assistance, working closely with the complaints section to provide legal advice and to monitor laws that affect consumers. For a village that cannot afford cou

rows.name: National Heritage Act — any person may nominate, and a neighbouring site can be designated to protect the one beside it
rows.desc_head: Any person may nominate. The heritage legislation of 2005 provides that any person may nominate to the Minister any natural heritage, any tangible or intangible cultural heritage, any living person or any underwater cultural heritage to be declared as National Heritage. The right is stated in those terms and is not confined to owners, councils or societies, which makes the nomination the si

rows.name: Land acquisition — your own valuer's fees can be reimbursed by the government, and the objection is Form N within six weeks
rows.desc_head: You may engage your own valuer, and the cost can be reimbursed by the government. The valuation and property services department, which advises the land administrator on compensation in acquisition cases, states in its own published account of the process that all persons interested can engage a private valuer and that the costs can be reimbursed by the government. For a household or a vill

rows.name: Forest Conservation Certificate — corporate money for keeping forest standing, on public land too, with results counted in hectares
rows.desc_head: A national fund that channels company money into keeping forest standing. The forest fund is an agency under the natural resources ministry, set up to develop and run financing instruments for forests. Its first instrument, launched in 2024, is the forest conservation certificate: a non-market mechanism through which private-sector money supports conservation projects, with results denomina

rows.name: Macaranga — a newsroom whose whole beat is the environment here, and which trains other newsrooms to cover it
rows.desc_head: A journalism portal whose only subject is this country's environment. Macaranga describes itself as a journalism portal covering the environment and sustainability in Malaysia, aiming to provide in-depth journalistic features on issues and to build knowledge about ecosystems. It is small and independent — run by its two co-founders, one a science journalist who has written for international

rows.name: Court judgment search — the government service that reaches published grounds of judgment, and the separate east Malaysian portal
rows.desc_head: There is a listed government service for finding judgments. The national digital services catalogue lists a court case judgment search that, in its own description, enables users to search, review and access court judgments and written grounds of judgment published by the Federal Court, the Court of Appeal, the High Court and other courts. That is the entry point worth starting from, becaus

rows.name: Land purchase funding through an international conservation funder working with local partners
rows.desc_head: An international funder that pays for land purchase, working through a local partner. The funder's own project page records that it and a local partner are working to purchase land to expand an existing national park in this country, with the local partner proposing that the new protected area — stated at 248,927 acres — be constituted as a state park. The site is described as lying within

rows.name: Mining leases and quarry approvals — the three-year documents a tenement holder must produce, and the official search at the state land office
rows.desc_head: A mineral tenement is granted first and the impact work comes after — and the holder may not operate until it is done. A state assembly's published answer on quarry approval procedure records that impact assessment is generally carried out only after the state authority has approved the mineral tenement in principle, and that the tenement holder is not permitted to carry out any development

rows.name: Kebenaran merancang — neighbouring owners get a served notice and twenty-one days to object with reasons, plus the local plan publicity and hearing
rows.desc_head: An adjoining landowner is served with notice and has twenty-one days to object. The planning control rules made under the town and country planning legislation contain the prescribed notice to a neighbouring owner, which states that it is to inform you of your right, as the owner of land adjoining the land to which the application relates, to object to that application within twenty-one day

rows.name: Perintah pemeliharaan pokok — a tree preservation order under the planning Act, the 0.8 metre rule that applies without one, and replacement on conviction
rows.desc_head: Cutting a tree whose girth exceeds 0.8 metres without the local authority's written permission is an offence in itself. The planning legislation contains a section prohibiting the cutting and similar treatment of a tree whose girth exceeds 0.8 metres, and a city council records prosecuting six people in the magistrates' court for felling two named trees with girths above that thresho

rows.name: State water authority — fifty-metre river reserves gazetted as protection zones, written permission for altering a water source, and directive letters and water protection orders against a polluting premises
rows.desc_head: A state water authority can gazette the river reserve itself as a protection zone. Answers tabled in a state assembly record that the water management board gazetted a named mukim as a protection zone under a stated subsection of its 1999 enactment in July 2009, to control activities in the river reserve, the buffer zone and the surrounding environment, including firefly habitat along a

rows.name: Fisheries Act 1985 and the fishing zones — Zone A reserved to traditional coastal fishers, the marine park written permission, and the licence-condition offence used against trawlers
rows.desc_head: The zoning system puts the first five nautical miles in the hands of coastal fishers. The state fisheries department records that the national fisheries waters zoning system has five zones — Zone A from nought to five nautical miles, Zone B from five to twelve, Zone C from twelve to thirty, and two outer zones — and that the Act is enforced to prevent conflict between coastal fish

rows.name: Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 — destroying the nest or eggs of a protected animal is its own offence, hunting within four hundred metres of a salt lick is another, and offences are arrestable
rows.desc_head: Destroying a nest or eggs is a separate, named offence, with a heavier penalty for the fully protected species. The 2010 wildlife conservation legislation provides that any person who damages or destroys the nest or eggs of protected wildlife commits an offence, punishable on conviction by a fine up to a stated amount or imprisonment up to one year or both, and that the same act a

rows.name: Standing in environmental judicial review — the "real and genuine interest" test the Federal Court settled, the case that stopped a retrospective exclusion, and the appeal provisions inside the Act
rows.desc_head: The standing test was settled in a 2014 case, and it is lower than proving a private right. Published reporting of a senior lawyer's account records that the biggest hurdle in public interest cases is locus standi — whether the party has a real and genuine interest and is adversely affected; that courts historically struck out cases where standing failed but have taken a much more

rows.name: MyEQMS — the department's public monitoring portal, the air pollutant index by station with its six pollutants and colour bands, and the parallel river and marine water quality index systems
rows.desc_head: One public portal carries the department's environmental monitoring, and it is filterable by state. The environment department runs a public portal under its environmental quality monitoring programme, with the air pollutant index management system giving the latest reading for each area with the time the reading was taken; guidance published for the public describes filtering

rows.name: Ecological Fiscal Transfers — federal money paid to states for gazetting and funding protected areas, the guideline setting allocation criteria, and the reporting that found most of it untraceable
rows.desc_head: Federal money is transferred to states specifically for conservation, and the purposes are stated. Published material records the transfer as a mechanism moving national funds to subnational governments based on conservation objectives and performance, its purpose being to encourage states to prioritise biodiversity conservation through terrestrial and marine protected areas, gaze

rows.name: The indigenous peoples' network and the rivers network — an umbrella of community organisations with three secretariats, community mapping training that has won legal cases, and the dam network beside it
rows.desc_head: An umbrella network of community organisations exists, with published addresses in three states. The 2009 environmental protection and management law provides that every person has the right to take part in environmental protection and management and to make a complaint arising from alleged pollution or damage to the environment. The ministerial regulation of 2017 on the procedure for managing complaints of

rows.name: Cek Berkas, Bhumi and Sentuh Tanahku — check the parcel, the file and the certificate without needing a name
rows.desc_head: Three public checks, run by the land ministry itself. The ministry publishes a file checking service, where entering the land office, the file number and the year returns the status of an application; an interactive land map carrying the geospatial data of the ministry's work units, with a parcel search; and a mobile application through which a certificate can be looked up, a parcel located

rows.name: Komisi Informasi — mediation that becomes a binding decision, and failure to publish is itself a dispute
rows.desc_head: Failure to publish is itself a ground of objection. A public body must respond to an information request within ten working days. The grounds on which an applicant may then object in writing include refusal of the request, information supplied incomplete, no response at all, information supplied outside the statutory period — and the non-provision of the periodic information that a public b

rows.name: Nusantara Atlas — clearance alerts tied to the concession, the mill and the village boundary
rows.desc_head: The alert is tied to the concession, so it names a company. The platform's dashboard links deforestation and fire alerts to the land-use layers that matter — palm oil, pulpwood and mining concessions, palm oil mills, protected areas and administrative boundaries all the way down to village level — and its own description is that this lets anyone quickly pinpoint the companies involved in fo

rows.name: Investigasi Bersama Tempo — a fellowship pairing local journalists with a national investigative desk, and a free manual
rows.desc_head: The programme pairs a local journalist with a national investigative desk. Published descriptions record a fellowship in which journalists from a range of media carry out an investigation jointly with the magazine's editorial team, receiving guidance and mentoring from reporters experienced in investigative work, with the stated aims of producing investigations, spreading investigative prac

rows.name: Badan Bank Tanah — at least thirty per cent for redistribution, ten-year use rights, and the route displaced communities have used
rows.desc_head: A state land body must set aside at least thirty per cent for redistribution. Established under a 2021 government regulation as a special status legal body created by central government with particular authority to manage land, it allocates a minimum of thirty per cent of the state land assigned to it for agrarian reform, with the allocation determined by the minister. Published figures for

rows.name: LPSK — statutory protection for a reporter or witness, and the one document the application turns on
rows.desc_head: A reporter, not only a witness, may apply. Under the witness and victim protection law of 2006 as amended in 2014, the agency may extend protection and other rights to witnesses, victims, reporters, cooperating suspects and experts, and its published answers record that an application may be lodged by the person concerned, by family, by a companion or legal counsel, by law enforcement offic

rows.name: Registered environmental laboratories — the published list, and why an unregistered lab's result cannot be used
rows.desc_head: Two things make a laboratory count here: accreditation and registration. The ministry's standards body defines an environmental laboratory as one holding an accreditation certificate for testing environmental quality parameters and for taking samples, together with a registration identity, and describes registration as the process of recording and recognising an already-accredited laborator

rows.name: Dana Desa — the village's own budget, with environmental conservation named, and the meeting where it is decided
rows.desc_head: Environmental conservation is a named use of the village's own money. Published summaries of the 2026 focus areas for the village fund include strengthening climate-resilient and disaster-resilient villages, with activities expressly covering waste management, environmental conservation, and the prevention of flooding and drought, alongside adaptation to floods, landslides, tidal flooding,

rows.name: Cagar Budaya registration — free to register, and protection attaches while the assessment is still running
rows.desc_head: Registration is free, and protection begins before any decision. Under the cultural heritage legislation and the implementing regulation of 2022, every person who owns or controls an object suspected of being cultural heritage must register it with the regent or mayor without charge, and anyone who finds such an object must report the find to the authority responsible for culture, to the po

rows.name: Pengadaan tanah — five forms of compensation, fourteen working days to object, and the remnant plot you can force them to take whole
rows.desc_head: Compensation is not only money. The land acquisition legislation of 2012 provides that compensation may be given in the form of money, replacement land, resettlement, share ownership, or another form agreed by both parties. A household that wants land rather than cash, or a community that wants resettlement together rather than individual payments, is therefore asking for something the stat

rows.name: Kitabisa — public donation platform open to communities, 5 per cent fee, verification required, and no politics
rows.desc_head: A community can open a public fundraising page here without being an organisation. The platform states that it facilitates anyone wishing to raise funds online and has been used by global non-governmental organisations, local foundations, communities, alumni associations, students and individuals. Creating a campaign page is free; the platform charges a five per cent administration fee on o

rows.name: MODI and MOMI — the national mining licence database and the concession map, searchable by commodity, location and licence status
rows.desc_head: Every mining licence holder must be registered in one national database. Published descriptions record that the mineral and coal directorate general's data system holds company data for mineral and coal operators including non-metallic minerals and rock, and that business entities and individuals holding the various classes of mining permit are required to be registered in it, with changes

rows.name: Posbakum and fee waiver — a legal help desk in every first-instance court, hearings held outside the court building, and the state paying the case costs
rows.desc_head: Three services exist for people who cannot afford to litigate, and they are set out in one supreme court regulation. Court pages explaining the 2014 supreme court regulation on legal services for people without means record three services across the general, religious and administrative court systems: a case cost waiver, under which the state bears the cost of the proceedings so that a pers

rows.name: Perhutanan sosial — five schemes for legal community management of state forest, thirty-five year approvals, and what the application must contain
rows.desc_head: There are five named schemes, and picking the right one is the whole task. rows.name: KKPR and the spatial plan — the conformity document every licensed activity needs, the two-year assessment, and the grounds for cancelling or revoking it
rows.desc_head: Every licensed activity must conform to the spatial plan, and the conformity itself is a document. The 2021 government regulation on spatial planning defines conformity of a space utilisation activity as the conformity between the planned activity and the spatial plan, and covers planning, utilisation and control — control including assessment of the implementation of that conformity, asses

rows.name: Coastal and small islands law — the right to propose the zoning plan, permits required of anyone using coastal resources, and customary law communities exempted from the permit
rows.desc_head: Communities have a statutory right to propose the plans that govern the coast. Published summaries of the coastal and small islands legislation record that it covers granting the community the right to propose the drafting of the strategic plan, the zoning plan, the management plan and the action plan for coastal and small islands management; the regulation of location permits and ma

rows.name: The 2024 conservation law — a new preservation-area category for important ecosystems outside protected areas, conservation as a duty of government and the public, and heavier penalties with ecosystem restoration
rows.desc_head: Important ecosystems outside the protected area system now have their own legal category. The 2024 law amending the 1990 conservation legislation defines a preservation area as an area outside nature reserve areas, nature conservation areas and the conservation areas in waters, coastal areas and small islands, whose ecological condition is maintained to support the life-support function

rows.name: The Supreme Court's environmental case guidelines — the decision that recognises class actions, organisation standing and citizen lawsuits, and the statutory articles each rests on
rows.desc_head: The Supreme Court issued guidelines for handling environmental cases, and they set out three routes side by side. The 2013 decision of the chief justice bringing into force the guidelines on handling environmental cases, published in the court's own legal documentation system, sets out the class action procedure and the citizen lawsuit or actio popularis, defining the latter and grou

rows.name: PROPER — the annual public rating of company environmental compliance, the five colour bands, and the black rating that follows deliberate pollution or refusal to obey an administrative sanction
rows.desc_head: Every rated company is placed in one of five public colour bands, and the ministry publishes the result. The environment ministry records that, to make company performance easy for the public to understand, compliance is grouped into five colour ratings — black for a company whose activities cause serious environmental impact but which does not carry out environmental management; red for

rows.name: HuMa and the People's Legal Companions — a network of trained non-lawyer legal companions working with communities on land and natural resources, its field school, and its conflict database
rows.desc_head: The organisation's central instrument is a network of trained companions who work with communities, not a litigation department. rows.name: ICEL and its landmark decisions portal — a searchable analysis of environmental judgments, an anti-SLAPP book aimed at the courts, and community empowerment as one of its three stated approaches
rows.desc_head: There is a portal of analysed environmental judgments, run by a law organisation rather than a court. The portal invites users to search analysis of environmental law decisions in the country, which is a different thing from the raw judgment database already recorded in this bucket: a community can read what a decision was held to mean, not only what it said. The organisation behind

rows.name: JATAM — a mining advocacy network of village, island and core nodes, provincial bodies with their own addresses, and its stated services from accompaniment to litigation
rows.desc_head: A network exists specifically for people living beside mines, and it is structured by node rather than by headquarters. The network records itself as a network of non-governmental and community organisations concerned with human rights, gender, environment, indigenous peoples and social justice issues in the mining and oil and gas industry, working with victim communities in many

rows.name: KIARA and the coastal advocacy team — a fisherfolk coalition founded by nine named organisations, its published Jakarta address, and the joint litigation team that sued a reclamation approval
rows.desc_head: Coastal and fishing communities have their own coalition, and its founders are named. The coalition records itself as a non-governmental organisation founded in 2002, initiated by nine civil society institutions focused on marine and fisheries issues, and lists those nine by name — a maritime association, a coastal development network, named foundations, a coast and sea network, a fi

rows.name: BRWA — the body where a community registers its mapped customary territory, why it was created, and the participatory mapping partners behind it
rows.desc_head: A mapped customary territory can be registered with a named body, and that body exists precisely because nobody else was keeping the record. The registration body records itself as the institution where customary territories are registered, formed in 2010 on the initiative of the indigenous peoples' alliance, a participatory mapping network, a forest watch organisation and a plant

rows.name: Auriga Nusantara — deforestation figures verified against satellite imagery and field visits, concession-level breakdowns naming who cleared what, and training for journalists and activists in the tracking tools
rows.desc_head: Deforestation here is counted by a civic foundation, concession by concession. Published reporting records its annual status report finding 261,575 hectares of natural forest lost in 2024, up 4,191 hectares on the previous year, and records that about 58.7 per cent — roughly 153,498 hectares — was inside company concessions, broken down as 36,068 hectares in logging concess

rows.name: The provincial accredited legal aid offices — the regional ministry list of every accredited office with its head and address, the poverty letter from the village head that opens the door, and the three-day answer rule
rows.desc_head: Each province's ministry office publishes the accredited legal aid organisations in that province, with names and addresses. rows.name: Village forest management bodies — formed by village deliberation, appointed by the village head's decision, with duties listed one by one, and the district facilitators who help them apply
rows.desc_head: A village forest body is created by the village's own regulation and its members appointed by the village head's decision. One village's published decision records the body established under a village regulation of 2018 on the formation of the village forest management body, appoints named office-holders as its committee, and lists their duties: strengthening the body; drawing up

rows.name: The village consultative body — a village-level legislature elected by territorial representation, whose agreement a village regulation needs, with thirteen listed tasks and a budget line of its own
rows.desc_head: A village regulation cannot pass without this body's agreement. rows.name: District and city land offices — the counter that re-marks a boundary on request, the complaint form that opens a dispute file, the receipt that proves it, and mediation before any court
rows.desc_head: A city land office publishes a service for re-marking a boundary, and the counter steps are listed. rows.name: Musrenbang — the annual village planning forum held by the fourth week of January, its four required forms, the sub-district delegates who escort a proposal upward, and the indicative budget ceiling announced at it
rows.desc_head: The village planning forum has a deadline and a paper trail. A village's own guidance records that the village planning forum is held every year, at the latest in the fourth week of January, and lists the administrative outputs that must be produced and reported to the sub-district as the minutes of the deliberation, a priority problems list form, a priority activities form and a

rows.name: Village-owned enterprises — a legal body the village creates by assembly decision and village regulation, capitalised from separated village wealth and from residents' own capital, to manage assets and natural resources
rows.desc_head: A village can create its own enterprise, and the decision is taken at the village assembly. A district community empowerment office records the 2014 village legislation as providing that a village may establish a village-owned enterprise; that it is managed in a spirit of kinship and mutual cooperation; and that it may run businesses in the economic field or in public services; and t

rows.name: Nature Society (Singapore) — the seat already at the agency table
rows.desc_head: Singapore offers no third-party objection route against a land-use decision, so the practical question is who is already in the room — and that is the NSS Conservation Committee, which states that it regularly takes part in engagements with the Housing and Development Board, JTC, the Land Transport Authority and the Public Utilities Board, and with private developers such as Mandai Wildlife

rows.name: Singapore Heritage Society — the other submission-writer, and what a Singapore campaign actually wins
rows.desc_head: Singapore has two organisations that write formal submissions on development, and this is the other one. Founded in 1987 as an independent non-profit, the Society works on rediscovering forgotten histories, sustaining living heritage such as the Pulau Ubin island community, cultural authenticity in districts such as Chinatown, and conservation of built heritage, particularly modern architec

rows.name: URA Master Plan — Singapore's leverage point is the five-yearly plan, not the individual application
rows.desc_head: Singapore gives an objector very little against a specific development, and a great deal against the designation that permits it. The Master Plan is the statutory land use plan under the Planning Act, guiding development over the next ten to fifteen years, reviewed every five years, and showing the permissible use and density for every parcel. Development that departs from it needs planning

rows.name: Legal Aid Bureau — advice without a merits test, and a provisional grant when proceedings are already running
rows.desc_head: Advice is much easier to obtain than representation, and most people never learn that. For legal advice the bureau applies only a preliminary means test — no merits test and no statement taking — with an appointment made through the ministry's portal to see the duty lawyer. rows.name: SAC-SINGLAS accreditation — a laboratory is accredited for specific tests only, which is the thing to check
rows.desc_head: Accreditation here means assessed technical competence, judged by peers. The national accreditation council administers the laboratory accreditation scheme, which assesses and recognises the technical competence and the management processes of a laboratory and its staff. Assessment works on a peer basis, with technical experts drawn from industry, government bodies and tertiary institutions

rows.name: SG Eco Fund — a year-round small grant and an annual large one, with two traps in the terms
rows.desc_head: Two doors, with very different burdens. The ministry's fifty million dollar fund, launched in November 2020, supports ground-up projects that involve the community and advance environmental sustainability, including climate change mitigation, waste reduction and the conservation of nature and biodiversity, and it takes applications from individuals, teams and organisations. rows.name: Reporting to NEA — an app that routes to the right agency, and a warning that you may be the witness
rows.desc_head: You do not have to know which agency is responsible. The national municipal feedback application routes a report to the relevant town council or agency, working across ten government agencies and seventeen town councils, and states in terms that the person reporting need not indicate which body is responsible. The environment agency's own feedback form performs the same triage in reverse: c

rows.name: INLIS land titles search — the registered owner from an address, and the pending instruments it will not show
rows.desc_head: The registered owner can be found from the address. The land authority states that the particulars of the registered owner of a private property can be obtained through the property ownership information service on its integrated land information portal, searchable by property address among other keys. The same portal sells survey plans and, drawing on three other agencies, road line plans,

rows.name: Bizfile — entity, people and industry searches, and what the free tier shows
rows.desc_head: Four searches, and two of them are unusual. The regulator's register offers four public search functions: entity, people, industry and reserved names. The industry search finds live businesses by their business activity — the authority's own example is finding all the active cafes in the country — and the people search follows individuals rather than companies. Nothing else recorded in this

rows.name: GeBIZ and the awarded contracts dataset — who won, for how much, and who else bid
rows.desc_head: One portal carries the public sector's tenders and quotations. The government's electronic procurement portal is where the public sector's invitations to quote and invitations to tender are posted, apart from security-sensitive contracts, with the tender documentation downloadable and bids submitted through the same system. Agencies also publish their annual procurement opportunities each y

rows.name: CPIB — the court must black out your name, and a government contract raises the stakes
rows.desc_head: The court itself must conceal the informer's identity. Under the protection of informers provision of the corruption act, complaints of an offence are not admissible in evidence in any civil or criminal proceeding, no witness is obliged or permitted to disclose the name or address of an informer or to state anything that might lead to their discovery, and where books or documents in evidenc

rows.name: Auditor-General's Office — checks that arise from complaints, and the follow-the-dollar audit
rows.desc_head: A complaint can start a check. The auditor-general's published report records that, alongside its planned audits, the office carried out checks arising from matters that came to its attention through observations from past audits, through feedback, and through complaints. Among the audit bodies recorded in this file, few say plainly that outside complaints feed the audit programme; here it

rows.name: Pro Bono SG — guidance clinics, and a non-litigation service for organisations including property matters
rows.desc_head: There is a service aimed at organisations, not only individuals. The legal guidance pages record support for non-profit organisations seeking legal guidance on non-litigation matters, and list property law — lease terms are the example given — among the fields covered, with a dedicated address for enquiries. A residents' committee, a registered society or a community group with a lease, a t

rows.name: Appraiser's licence and the surveyors' institute — only licensed appraisers may value land, and every licence expires in December
rows.desc_head: Valuing land here requires a licence. The revenue authority states plainly that anyone who appraises lands and buildings in the country must apply for an appraiser's licence. The first check on any valuation put in front of a household is therefore whether the person who signed it holds one, and that is a narrower and more answerable question than whether they are qualified or experienced.

rows.name: Environmental studies — published reports, a roughly month-long window, and proximity to a sensitive area as the trigger
rows.desc_head: Proximity to a sensitive area is the trigger. The planning authority's own account records that proposed development projects near sensitive areas — nature reserves, nature areas, marine and coastal areas, other areas of significant biodiversity, or projects with potential trans-boundary impact — are subject to greater scrutiny, with the technical agencies for parks, environment, ports and

rows.name: National monument preservation — open spaces now qualify, a notice of intention is published, and an enforcement notice can stop work
rows.desc_head: Open spaces and inland waters can now be preserved, not only buildings. The preservation legislation originally allowed the preservation of buildings and structures and of sites containing the remains of one. rows.name: Land acquisition compensation — the inquiry where you file your claim, and the assessors you may object to
rows.desc_head: The inquiry is where a claim is filed, and it has a date on the notice. Acquisition is governed by the land acquisition legislation and administered by the land authority, which states that owners whose land is acquired are paid market value compensation. rows.name: Garden City Fund — the charity money route into conservation on state green space, with a 2.5 times tax deduction
rows.desc_head: Where land cannot be bought, this is the money route. Almost all green space here is state land, so the acquisition question a community faces elsewhere becomes a funding question: how to put money and effort into protecting a specific habitat that is not yours. The parks board established a registered charity with institution of a public character status, managed independently as a charity

rows.name: Jom — a subscriber-funded weekly that runs essays taking months, in a media landscape where long-form is rare
rows.desc_head: A reader-funded magazine that publishes on a fixed weekly rhythm. Founded in 2022, Jom describes itself as a weekly digital magazine covering arts, culture, politics, business and technology in Singapore, independent and with no affiliation to any party, corporate interest or organisation, run by three co-founders. rows.name: Fund-raising permits — the police licence, the charity exemption, the seven-day disclosure and the unmanned-box carve-out
rows.desc_head: Whether you need a police licence depends on who benefits, not on what you are raising for. House to house and street collections remain licensed by the police, except where the collection is by or for a registered or exempt charity, or is a foreign-purposes appeal by a person approved by the charities commissioner. rows.name: Tree conservation areas and the Heritage Tree scheme — one metre of girth needs written approval, five metres and anyone can nominate
rows.desc_head: Inside a tree conservation area, felling a mature tree needs written approval even with no development going on. The parks agency records that developers and private property owners wishing to fell any mature tree with a girth exceeding one metre must seek written approval from the Commissioner of Parks and Recreation, even if no developmental works are currently in progress. Published data

rows.name: Planning permission — provisional versus written permission, the two-year validity, the exemption list, and the status check anyone can run
rows.desc_head: Work cannot lawfully begin until the final permission is in hand, and the two stages have different names. The planning authority records that planning permission is required for development and building works including changing the use of premises, that some proposals can be registered under plan lodgment for instant approval, and that an exemption list sets out works needing no permission

rows.name: Construction noise control — the no-work rule within 150 metres, noise meters the contractor must install at your building, and the limits that tighten at night
rows.desc_head: The contractor has to put noise meters at the nearest affected buildings — which may be yours. rows.name: Earth Control Measures — silty discharge from a construction site is reportable to a 24-hour line, with CCTV on larger sites and prosecutions on record
rows.desc_head: Silty water running off a construction site into a drain is a reportable offence, and the reporting line is published. rows.name: Marine park protection under the parks legislation — fishing, coral collection and mooring made offences without approval, and the jurisdiction gap that made the amendment necessary
rows.desc_head: Adding a marine park to the parks legislation made three specific acts offences without approval. The parliamentary record of the 2017 amendment states that by adding a definition of marine park and adding it as a type of public park, the protection of the parks legislation is applied to the designated foreshore as well as the marine areas of the marine park — so that it is an offence to

rows.name: Nature reserves and nature park networks — the four reserves conserved by statute, the buffer parks around them, and the offence of releasing animals into watercourses that flow in
rows.desc_head: Four nature reserves are conserved under the parks legislation, and the largest doubles as the water catchment. The parks agency records that the country's four nature reserves are conserved under the parks and trees legislation, are primary providers of ecosystem services helping clean air and water, and hold native flora and fauna including rare and endangered species; that the lar

rows.name: The wetland reserve and its nature park network — gazettement under the parks legislation, a 400-hectare network built on ecological connectivity research, and enforcement teeth against poaching
rows.desc_head: The decision to safeguard the buffer habitats was made on ecological connectivity research, and the agency says so. rows.name: The public consultation portal — every ministry's open consultations in one place, roughly four weeks each, with the summary of responses published afterwards
rows.desc_head: Every ministry's consultations are posted in one place, and feedback goes straight to the agency. rows.name: OneMap and the open data portal — the national map with over a hundred thematic layers and a public API, and datasets published in mapping formats under an open licence
rows.desc_head: The national map publishes its interfaces for members of the public, not only for agencies. rows.name: The wider nature movement — the campaigns that got a reclamation deferred and a rail alignment reopened, the roundtable where groups and agencies meet, and the volunteer groups a resident can join
rows.desc_head: Campaigns here have changed decisions, and the record names which ones. rows.name: The natural history museum's reference collections — specimens catalogued with collection dates and locations, a herbarium of the region's plants, and a hundred thousand field notes and photographs
rows.desc_head: The national reference collection is the record of what used to live where. rows.desc_head: When clearance starts on a site, displaced animals need a number that answers, and this is it. rows.name: The specialist species societies and the sector directory — a volunteer herpetological society that runs surveys and holds a student grant, and a published list of the country's nature and environment organisations
rows.desc_head: Specialist volunteer societies exist for particular groups of animals, and they do survey work. rows.desc_head: There is a private firm whose ordinary business is restoring habitat, and its services are listed. rows.desc_head: Volunteers patrol the rivers here on a fixed schedule, and the society has offices inside the parks. rows.name: The free legal clinic directory and the regulator's lawyer search — clinics listed by region with addresses, hours and eligibility, and a searchable database of every registered solicitor by practice area
rows.desc_head: Every free legal clinic in the country is listed in one place, sorted by region. Its entries show how narrow

rows.name: Town councils and the municipal coordination office — seventeen estate-level bodies that control common property and keep their own accounts, and the reporting route that names which one is responsible
rows.desc_head: Seventeen estate-level bodies control the common property residents live on, and their duties are published. rows.desc_head: Five district councils sit between residents and the government, and they design their own schemes. rows.desc_head: The Code replaces the patchwork, and public participation is named among its principles. rows.name: Reporting waste and unclearanced projects — five places to report, and a tenfold penalty

rows.name: PAVA compensation rates — the 120-day notice, the published adjustment factors, and the banks' rival rate

rows.name: Civil Society Organizations Authority — the two categories, the endowment thresholds, and the offence of unlawful collection
rows.desc_head: Registration is the gateway, and there are only two categories. rows.desc_head: A national legal aid centre exists, and the limits on what it provides are stated. rows.desc_head: The 2023 rules set out what a community forest management group must produce and what it gets in return. rows.desc_head: A dedicated legal entity finances the protected area network, and its goals are published.
